_about: Hand-constructed hazard cases for IFEval's PlaceholderChecker (detectable_content:number_placeholders). The checker counts EVERY square-bracket span as a 'placeholder' via re.findall(r'\[.*?\]', value); the instruction only asks for fill-in placeholders 'such as [address]'. 'expected_upstream'/'expected_intended' are outcomes reasoned by hand BEFORE the machine run (see prereg.md); test_ifeval_placeholder_hazards.py asserts the machine reproduces them. Outcomes PASS/FAIL (this checker never raises). INTENDED = a conservative count that excludes inline/reference links, reference/footnote definitions, footnote refs, task-list checkboxes and pure-numeric citations, and uses re.DOTALL. CC BY 4.0.

cases.note: Two inline markdown links. Upstream counts [OpenAI] and [Google] = 2 >= 2 -> PASS. Intended: both spans are followed by '(' (link anchors), so 0 genuine placeholders -> 0 >= 2 is FAIL. A response with no fill-in placeholder is scored as following the instruction.

cases.value: The model scores well [1]. Prior work agrees [2]. See also [3].
cases.note: Three numeric citation markers. Upstream counts [1],[2],[3] = 3 >= 3 -> PASS. Intended: inner is all digits for each, so excluded; 0 genuine placeholders -> FAIL.
A GitHub task list. Upstream counts [x],[ ],[ ] = 3 >= 2 -> PASS. Intended: inner is 'x'/' '/' ' (checkbox tokens), all excluded; 0 genuine placeholders -> FAIL.

cases.note: Two footnote references. Upstream counts [^1],[^2] = 2 >= 2 -> PASS. Intended: inner starts with '^' (footnote), excluded; 0 genuine placeholders -> FAIL.

cases.note: Two genuine placeholders that each wrap a line break. The upstream pattern has no re.DOTALL, so '.' cannot cross '\n' and neither span matches -> count 0 >= 2 is FAIL. Intended (DOTALL) counts both = 2 >= 2 -> PASS. The same regex is both too broad (brackets in links) and too narrow (no DOTALL).
